primitives.verbatim_quote: The authors propose Kernel Rank Centrality (KRC): a spectral estimator that kernel-smooths binary outcomes over time into a Markov transition matrix and reads item strengths from its stationary distribution.

reasoning_traces.think:
KRC constructs a time-varying Markov transition matrix P(t) from binary outcomes y_ij(t) via kernel smoothing. Its stationary distribution π(t) encodes item strengths. The spectral approach ensures convergence to π(t) via power iteration. The group-inverse approximation enables closed-form inference of π(t) and its variance. The online update mechanism uses Sherman–Morrison formula to efficiently adjust π(t) upon new observations. This avoids costly full re-estimation and supports real-time inference. Failure modes include loss of irreducibility, bandwidth selection issues, and numerical instability in group inverse computation. The method bridges discrete pairwise comparisons with continuous strength dynamics, offering a principled way to forecast time-varying rankings.
